analysis_md:
# SOLV — Solventum Corporation
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-17. Market cap $15.042B at $85.81 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or segments.json — none are recomputed. Research findings from web sources are paraphrased and labelled as such.

## What it is
The former 3M health care business, spun off on April 1, 2024. Three reportable segments after the September 2025 divestiture (segments.json, FY2025 revenue): MedSurg $4,817,000,000 (57.9% of sales, +3.88% YoY) — advanced wound care (incl. V.A.C. negative-pressure therapy) and infection prevention / surgical solutions; Health Information Systems $1,360,000,000 (16.3%, +4.13%) — 360 Encompass revenue-cycle and coding software; Dental Solutions $1,349,000,000 (16.2%, +4.17%) — Filtek restoratives and orthodontics. Purification & Filtration contributed a $497,000,000 stub in FY2025 before its sale to Thermo Fisher Scientific closed on September 2, 2025 for $4.0 billion in cash before customary adjustments, with net proceeds of $3.4 billion used primarily to pay down debt (company release, paraphrased). All Other (drinking-water filtration, product supplied to 3M) was $302,000,000. In Q2 2026 the company announced it plans to separate HIS as well, and it closed the Acera acquisition in December 2025 (acquisitions of $696,000,000 in FY2025, fundamentals.json).

## Owner's earnings
**Filed history (financials_history.csv):** revenue $8,130,000,000 (FY2022) → $8,197,000,000 → $8,254,000,000 → $8,325,000,000 (FY2025) — under 1% a year as reported. Conservative owner's earnings (OCF − capex − SBC): $1,391,000,000 / $1,586,000,000 / $693,000,000 / −$171,000,000; per share $8.05 / $9.18 / $3.99 / −$0.98. OE positive in 3 of the last 4 years. The maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) prints $1,670,000,000 / $1,617,000,000 / $1,267,000,000 / $1,805,000,000 — but its FY2025 figure runs through net income, which contains the divestiture gain (below), so the maintenance version is the flattered one here and the OCF-based conservative series is the cleaner lens.

**Why the history is not one clean series — the basis break.** FY2022–23 are 3M carve-out years: no standalone debt (net debt −$194,000,000 in FY2023), SBC of only $37,000,000–$39,000,000 a year on 3M's allocation, and no standalone interest burden. The spin loaded the balance sheet in FY2024 (total debt $8,010,000,000; SG&A stepped from 28.0% of revenue in FY2023 to 33.7% in FY2024 and 37.0% in FY2025, fundamentals.json) and SBC stepped to $112,000,000 then $161,000,000. The carve-out OE/share of $8–9 is not a run rate for the standalone company and is never used as one below.

**Base used = the engine's normalized base, median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $3.989637305699482/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the median year is FY2024). It is the first standalone year, earned with the full debt load and P&F still owned for the full year — imperfect, but the only filed year that is neither carve-out nor divestiture-distorted.

**TTM — run, quoted, and NOT used as the base.** ttm.py (filing-direct) legs through Q2 2026:
- OCF: FY $369,000,000 − prior YTD $198,000,000 + current YTD $38,000,000 = **TTM $209,000,000**
- Capex: FY $379,000,000 − prior YTD $219,000,000 + current YTD $167,000,000 = **TTM $327,000,000**
- SBC: FY $161,000,000 − prior YTD $83,000,000 + current YTD $89,000,000 = **TTM $167,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **174,400,000**
- **TTM OE total −$285,000,000 → TTM OE/share −$1.6341743119266054**

Pinning the base to −$1.63 would print a Tier F. That reading is rejected as the base for a documented reason: the TTM window sits exactly on the separation-cost peak. Management's own framing (Q4 2025 guidance call, paraphrased from search results) is that reported FY2026 free cash flow of roughly $200 million would be closer to $1 billion excluding separation costs, payments due to 3M and divestiture-support costs, with separation costs stepping down significantly in 2027 as the separation completes; Q1 2025 reporting likewise attributed the OCF drop to planned payments, separation costs and interest timing, and Q3 2025 reporting put year-to-date free cash flow excluding separation and divestiture costs at a 93% conversion rate. H1 2026 GAAP cash generation also absorbed litigation-related charges and ERP-cutover costs (Q2 2026 reporting, paraphrased). Those are real cash costs today — they are why the verdict below is sized to the conservative end and why the TTM result is carried as the F end of the method range — but they are contractually winding down (roughly 70% of transition service agreements exited by Q2 2026, per the same reporting), so a permanent-capitalization of the trough year would be a spurious F, the same pattern as the rejected TTM bases in the ADM/BG/ARES passes. The TTM figure is disclosed, not hidden: on it, there is no positive OE to discount.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: category leadership and recurring consumables, but measured returns and margins do not clear a wider bar. Gross margin fell every year on file — 57.7% (FY2022) → 57.3% → 55.6% → 53.5% (FY2025), 54.7% on the TTM in fundamentals.json. The ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) ran 11.5% (FY2022) and 11.9% (FY2023) on a carve-out capital base, fell to 8.0% in FY2024, and prints 21.5% in FY2025 only because reported operating income of $2,181,000,000 contains the Purification & Filtration gain (the Q3 2025 cash-flow statement backs a $1,518,000,000 gain on sale of business out of net income; the gain sits in operating income per the company's non-GAAP reconciliations — sources paraphrased).
- FOR: #1 advanced wound care position (V.A.C. negative-pressure wound therapy) with recurring consumables pull-through; premium dental restorative brands (Filtek) and orthodontic franchise with dentist familiarity / switching friction; HIS 360 Encompass revenue-cycle platform embedded in hospital coding and billing workflows — real switching costs; regulatory-cleared portfolio, hospital channel relationships and materials IP (owned for its field of use) inherited from 3M; diversified recurring-revenue mix (MedSurg 57.9% / HIS 16.3% / Dental 16.2% of FY2025 sales).
- AGAINST: gross-margin erosion of ~4pp in three years — cost, mix, the 3M supply-agreement markup and tariffs have beaten pricing power so far; underlying ROIC proxy of 8.0% in FY2024 is at, not well above, the cost of capital; contested in every segment (Medtronic / Smith+Nephew in wound care, Dentsply Sirona / Envista in dental, Oracle Health in HIS, per search-result summaries) with pricing pressure in surgical supplies; the 3M long-term supply agreement gives the supplier a 2027 option to raise certain raw-material costs, disclosed as a possible ~100bp margin headwind; the planned HIS separation removes the stickiest software asset, and reported revenue growth on file is under 1% a year.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4 final run (2026-10-17)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended start is 0.29% (g_base 0.002937961323730809), built from reported revenue — a series dragged by the divested P&F stub and the flat carve-out years. The continuing business is printing faster: FY2025 segment growth was +3.88% / +4.13% / +4.17% across MedSurg / HIS / Dental (segments.json), Q2 2026 normalized organic growth was estimated by management at about 4% after removing roughly $125 million of ERP-related advance orders from the reported print, and FY2026 organic guidance was raised to +2.5–3.0% (+3.5–4.0% excluding SKU exits) alongside adjusted EPS guidance of $7.10–$7.20 and free-cash-flow guidance of $200–$300 million (Q2 2026 release, paraphrased). Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.092938 / −0.022938 / +0.027062 / +0.077062 / +0.147062 vs g_base) to −9 / −2 / **+3** / +8 / +15%: the base start sits on the guided organic rate, the bull start assumes the separation-cost roll-off converts revenue growth into faster OE/share growth, and even the super-bull start is an OE-normalization story off a trough base — it is below the OE/share swing the filed history itself produced between FY2023 and FY2024, so it is not a revenue heroics case. Sanity check against prints: no scenario start contradicts a reported revenue print once the divestiture drag is accounted for, and the bear/super-bear starts cover a failed normalization. Probabilities were skewed bear-ward to 15/30/30/15/10 (45% on bear-or-worse) because the latest FY and the TTM are both negative on the conservative definition and the balance sheet is levered; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $85.81.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −9.0% | 0.75 | Separation drag persists, 3M cost step-up lands, margins keep eroding | $15.15 | 4.39% |
| Bear | 30% | −2.0% | 0.90 | Slow normalization; cash conversion stays weak through 2027 | $24.40 | 5.90% |
| Base | 30% | +3.0% | 1.00 | Guided organic growth; separation costs roll off on schedule | $33.40 | 7.38% |
| Bull | 15% | +8.0% | 1.10 | Roll-off plus Acera / new-product momentum lifts OE/share faster than sales | $45.21 | 9.28% |
| Super bull | 10% | +15.0% | 1.25 | Full normalization to pre-trough cash conversion at a higher margin | $68.46 | 12.71% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $33.24 (−61.3% vs price), IV@12% $43.94, IV@10% $55.86, weighted IRR 7.41%, base-case IRR 7.38%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D, bull D — no band split). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 4.65%, terminal value 18.27% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.52x, net debt 5.94x normalized OE, 9.53 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and its full legs are quoted above. The TTM base (−$1.63/share) was NOT pinned, for the documented separation-peak reason stated in the Owner's earnings section; the median base is used and the TTM result is carried as the F end of the method range. Post-FY evidence (Q2 2026: guidance raised, normalized organic growth ~4%) is reflected in the recalibrated scenario starts rather than in a hand-built base.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and OCF differ by >40% in 2024, 2025): identified, two different one-offs. FY2025: net income of $1,556,000,000 contains the $1,518,000,000 pre-tax gain on the P&F sale (Q3 2025 cash-flow statement, paraphrased source), which is investing cash, not operating cash — reported operating income and the maintenance OE definition are flattered by it, the conservative OCF-based series is not. FY2024: net income of $479,000,000 vs OCF of $1,185,000,000 is the spin year — separation costs, the new standalone interest burden and carve-out tax allocations hit earnings ahead of cash. Consequence: the verdict rests on the conservative series only.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share −$0.98 vs 3-yr median $3.99): both ends are distorted, in opposite directions. The latest FY is the trough: OCF of $369,000,000 absorbed peak separation and divestiture costs in the year the P&F cash contribution left. The median ($3.99, FY2024) is the least-distorted filed year — first standalone year, full debt load — but it still includes a full year of the now-sold P&F business and a partial year of separation costs. The median is used as the standardized base, the latest/TTM are disclosed as the F end of the range, and probabilities are skewed bear-ward to charge for the distortion.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.52x super-bear IV): real — the outcome genuinely hinges on whether separation costs roll off as guided. Confidence is low (and would be capped at medium by rule in any case); the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 5.94x normalized OE): stated from the filing — total debt $5,035,000,000 (all long-term at FY2025), cash $878,000,000, net debt $4,157,000,000, plus lease liabilities of $212,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json). Leverage is down from $8,010,000,000 of gross debt at FY2024 thanks to the P&F proceeds, and buybacks have begun ($355,000,000 of repurchases in H1 2026, fundamentals.json dividends block), but at 5.9x the normalized OE base a failed normalization squeezes equity value fast — this is priced into the 45% bear-or-worse weight.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range: on the normalized median base ($3.99/share) this run prints Tier D (weighted IRR 7.41%, IV@15% $33.24); on the latest-FY base (−$0.98) and the TTM base (−$1.63) there is no positive conservative OE at all — Tier F. The preliminary default run (median base, default probabilities/offsets) printed 7.18% / $32.08, also D, so the recalibration did not manufacture the verdict. Every defensible input set fails the 15% hurdle at $85.81 by a wide margin: even the super-bull scenario alone yields only a 12.71% IRR.
- The bull story is real but it is a normalization story, not a DCF story at this price: separation costs roll off in 2027, HIS separates, Acera compounds, buybacks shrink the count.
